summary: The ID.5 is the coupe-liftback body of Volkswagen's ID.4, sold in Australia in only two grades - the 210kW rear-drive Pro and the 250kW dual-motor GTX 4Motion - both on the same MEB platform and 82-84kWh battery. Australian reviewers rate the Pro highly for real-world efficiency and ride refinement, with several calling it one of the better-driving mid-size electric SUVs, but they are close to unanimous that the GTX's $10,000 premium buys less range than it costs and that the sloping roof and haptic controls cost the car genuine practicality. Both grades list under the $75,000 FBT exemption cap, though the GTX clears it by only $2,010 before dealer delivery or options.
pros: The Pro lists at $62,990 for 543km WLTP from a 77kWh usable pack, $3,000 more than the ID.4 Pro but $4,000 under a Skoda Enyaq Coupe 85 Sportline ($66,990) with almost identical range

Beats its own efficiency claim in Australian conditions: CarsGuide's long-term Pro averaged 15.8kWh/100km against a 16.3kWh/100km claim, and carsales recorded 16.1kWh/100km in the GTX against 16.9kWh/100km claimed

Tows well clear of its MEB siblings: 1,200kg braked on the Pro and 1,800kg on the dual-motor GTX 4Motion (rated at a 12 per cent gradient), against 1,000-1,200kg for a Skoda Enyaq and 1,000-1,200kg for an Audi Q4 e-tron
Cheap scheduled maintenance: 2-year/30,000km service intervals with a prepaid 10-year/150,000km plan at $2,890 - about $289 a year - alongside an 8-year/160,000km battery warranty
GTX adds 250kW dual-motor 4Motion, 5.4s to 100km/h and a rear-biased torque split sending up to 80 per cent to the back axle, and CarsGuide rated the chassis 'resolved, refined' at 7.5/10
cons: The $72,990 GTX gives up 21km of range to the $62,990 Pro (522km v 543km) for 0.9s of 0-100km/h; both CarExpert and CarsGuide judge it the worse buy of the two

The coupe roofline is a real practicality cost, not just a style choice - CarsGuide's long-termer found child-seat installation awkward and tall loads won't fit, and folded volume drops to 1,561L against the ID.4's 1,575L

Haptic and touch controls for climate and volume draw consistent criticism (CarsGuide: they 'sometimes work and sometimes don't'), and there is no frunk, no vehicle-to-load and no vehicle-to-grid at either grade
The GTX sits only $2,010 under the $75,000 FBT exemption cap on list price, so dealer delivery plus one option can push a novated lease past the threshold the Pro clears comfortably
Five-star ANCAP rating is carried over from 2021 Euro NCAP testing of the pre-facelift ID.4, with no fresh local assessment of the updated car
